title: Zero Lot Line
summary: Lets two neighbouring houses share the space between them (one wall at or near the property line, the other 1.5 m back) instead of each meeting the soffit limits of Sentences 9.10.15.5.(8) and (9) on its own. It works only if both houses are built to these conditions and an access agreement is registered on both titles.

source.title: City of Calgary, Variance SPV-001 Zero Lot Line (Revision 5, 5 March 2026)

groups.plain: Check these first. If one does not fit your project, the package cannot be used as published.

groups.title: Walls, soffits and finishes on both houses

groups.title: Windows, vents and openings

groups.title: Wiring, services and decorative returns
groups.plain: What can go inside or on the wall near the property line.

groups.title: Registered access agreement (MARW)
groups.plain: The Maintenance Access Right of Way agreement on the titles of both parcels.

groups.title: Permit documents
groups.plain: How the package is tied to your building permit.

conditions.subject: both_parcels
conditions.plain: Each lot provides a 1.5 m maintenance easement. A side facing a street or lane may not need one, but a side next to a zero-lot-line neighbour always does.

source.label: l) i.
source.quote: Each lot must provide a 1.5 m Maintenance Easement Agreement, except for lots terminating at a street or lane

conditions.subject: both_houses
conditions.plain: No soffit projects more than 0.3 m into the easement.

source.label: l) ii.
source.quote: Maximum allowable soffit projection into the easement: 0.3 m.

conditions.subject: both_houses
conditions.plain: No footing projects more than 0.3 m into the easement. Note: page 5 of the source says the agreement can allow 0.6 m; ask the City which figure applies.

source.label: l) iii.
source.quote: Maximum allowable footing projection into the easement: 0.3 m.
source.diagram: Sample Cross Section Detail of Adjacent Zero Lot Line Houses, p.6 ("0.3 m allowable footing projection into the easement")

conditions.subject: both_parcels
conditions.plain: The easement stays clear of anything that could get in the way of firefighting. Side entrance steps and landings no more than 0.6 m above or below grade, without guards, do not count as obstructions.

source.label: l) iv.
source.quote: easement on a Zero Lot Line build shall remain clear of all obstructions which could impede firefighting efforts.

conditions.subject: both_parcels
conditions.plain: The MARW agreement, in a form the City accepts, is registered on the title of your parcel and of the adjacent parcel.

source.label: Authority and conditions
source.quote: must be registered on the title of th parcel and the adjacent parcel over a 1.5m width parallel to the property line.
source.lead_in: A Maintenance Access Right of Way (MARW) agreement in a form satisfactory to the Authority Having Jurisdiction (City of Calgary)

conditions.subject: both_parcels
conditions.plain: Any projection across the property line stays within what the agreement allows: eaves up to 0.3 m, footings up to 0.6 m (page 4 says 0.3 m for footings; ask the City).

source.label: Authority and conditions
source.quote: The agreement can allow for 0.3 m eave projection and a 0.6m footing projection across the property line.

conditions.subject: both_houses
conditions.plain: No part of the two buildings, eaves included, is ever closer than 0.9 m to the other.

source.label: Authority and conditions
source.quote: At no time may any portion of the buildings including the eaves on either parcel be closer together than 0.9 m.
source.diagram: Sample Cross Section Detail of Adjacent Zero Lot Line Houses, p.6 ("Minimum distance of 0.9 m between facias c/w with unvented soffit")

conditions.subject: permit_documents
conditions.plain: Your building permit documents name SPV-001. Naming it is how the owner or contractor accepts the authority it is issued under.

source.label: Authority and conditions
source.quote: The owner/contractor acknowledging the authority under which the variance is issued by virtue of referencing this Variance number (SPV-001) in the Building Permit documentation.

conditions.subject: permit_documents
conditions.plain: The conditions of the issued building permit name SPV-001. The City writes these; check them when the permit is issued.

source.label: This Variance is based on
source.quote: Reference to this variance within the permit conditions of the building permit.

conditions.subject: project
conditions.plain: The owner and the contractor make sure the project is built as the package sets out.

source.label: Authority and conditions
source.quote: The owner, and contractor ensuring that the project is carried out as outlined in this Variance.

source_notes.plain: The source gives two footing projections: 0.3 m into the easement on page 4 (and in the page 6 figure) and 0.6 m across the property line on page 5. Only the City can say which applies.
source_notes.quote: The agreement can allow for 0.3 m eave projection and a 0.6m footing projection across the property line.

source_notes.plain: The sample cross-section on page 6 also notes that unprotected openings serving the same room are kept at least 2.0 m from other unprotected openings. That note is only in the figure, not in the written conditions; ask the City whether it applies.
If you rely on this package to get a permit, not meeting its requirements is an offence under the Safety Codes Act.
source_notes.quote: If this variance is relied upon to obtain a permit, non-compliance with the requirements of this variance are an offence under the Safety Codes Act.
